Aufgaben
  
  
At Mercedes-Benz Research & Development North America (MBRDNA), we are committed to delivering world-class automotive technologies that push the boundaries of what is possible. Our teams of highly skilled engineers and designers use cutting-edge software and technology, to enhance the driving experience and reduce environmental impact.
  
  
Position Overview
  
  
As Mercedes-Benz scales ADAS across production fleets, the US ADAS Data & Forensics team is building applied-AI capabilities that go beyond descriptive KPI reporting. These capabilities include vision-language models that analyze SSR Scene Safety Recording footage, LLM-based event classification and reasoning, embedding-based semantic retrieval over driving scenarios, automated scenario discovery, natural-language event descriptions, and model-based ranking that surfaces the most important events from thousands of daily drives. As a Data Scientist, you will develop and deploy these capabilities in production for two stakeholder groups: management, through fleet-performance summaries, trend forecasts, and AI-generated event narratives; and engineers, through granular model-assisted analysis of ADAS calibration, scenarios, edge cases, and behavioral patterns across road types, weather, firmware, and driver cohorts.
  
  
Relocation assistance (domestic or international) is not provided for this position.
  
  
**Job Responsibilities**

* Apply vision-language models to SSR video and combine video analysis with structured telemetry to create multimodal event representations.
* Build LLM classification and reasoning pipelines that triage events by severity and root cause and generate human-readable summaries of takeovers, safety events, and deactivations.
* Design embedding pipelines and semantic search for similar-event retrieval, and develop unsupervised clustering methods that discover recurring scenarios and edge-case families at fleet scale.
* Build model-based ranking and scoring systems that reduce manual event triage, develop active-learning loops using engineer feedback, and proactively detect fleet-level anomalies.
* Quantify the impact of firmware updates and configuration changes on KPIs, segment driver cohorts, and design A/B and quasi-experimental frameworks.
* Analyze campaign effectiveness, build coverage-optimization models, and develop automated fleet-quality scoring.
* Deploy models into PySpark and Delta Lake pipelines and the FastAPI analytics API, build evaluation frameworks for foundation-model outputs, and operate on the Azure data platform, including ADLS, Synapse, and Container Apps.

Qualifikationen
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Data Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field. A Master's degree or PhD is beneficial but not required; demonstrated experience carries equal weight.
* 3+ years of professional experience.
* 2-5 years of experience in data science or applied machine learning.
* Depth in at least one of the following: applied foundation models such as LLMs, VLMs, or embeddings; classical machine learning in production; or statistical experimentation.
* Strong Python skills using NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn, with an emphasis on clean, testable code, and strong SQL skills.
* Experience with ML model development, including feature engineering, model selection, and evaluation on real data.
* Solid statistics knowledge, including hypothesis testing, regression, and experimental design.
* Ability to communicate findings clearly to engineers and management through reports, presentations, and dashboards.
* Ability to turn ambiguous questions into structured analytical approaches.

**Strongly Preferred**

* LLM or VLM application experience, including prompt engineering, structured outputs, and evaluation.
* Embedding models and vector similarity for retrieval or clustering.
* PySpark for large-scale processing; candidates with strong pandas experience may ramp up.
* Time-series analysis or anomaly detection.

**Nice To Have**

* Multimodal foundation models applied to video or image data.
* RAG or vector-database systems such as FAISS, pgvector, or Pinecone.
* Spatial or geospatial clustering with DBSCAN or HDBSCAN.
* Ranking or recommendation systems, active learning, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.
* Delta Lake or Parquet; FastAPI or model-serving APIs; MLOps platforms such as MLflow or Weights & Biases.
* Cloud-platform experience in Azure, AWS, or GCP.
* Vehicle telemetry or automotive-domain experience; campaign analytics or A/B testing at scale.
* Data privacy, including CCPA or GDPR, for vehicle data and foundation models.
* English required; German is an advantage.

**About The Role**
As a Machine Learning Engineer 5, you will develop the infrastructure and production systems that power machine learning applications at scale. Working primarily with Python and Kubernetes, you will help support real-time services used by millions of customers throughout their relationship with Capital One. The role connects machine learning, software engineering, operations, and data engineering. Design, build, and deliver machine learning models, services, and components in partnership with product and data science teams. Build and optimize data pipelines for training, evaluation, and production inference. Deploy, retrain, maintain, and monitor models and services in cloud environments, using container orchestration and distributed computing technologies where appropriate. **About The Role**
What if your expertise in machine learning, statistical inference, and data engineering could directly shape how the world's most advanced AI systems reason and problem-solve? We're looking for Masters-level data scientists to challenge, evaluate, and refine cutting-edge AI models — stress-testing their reasoning on the hardest problems your field has to offer.
  
  
This is a fully remote, flexible contract role. No prior AI industry experience needed — just deep domain knowledge and a sharp eye for technical accuracy.
  
  

* Organization: Alignerr
* Type: Hourly Contract
* Location: Remote
* Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

**What You'll Do**

* Design Advanced Challenges — Create rigorous data science problems spanning hyperparameter optimization, Bayesian inference, cross-validation strategies, dimensionality reduction, and more
* Author Ground-Truth Solutions — Write precise, step-by-step technical solutions including Python/R scripts, SQL queries, and mathematical derivations that serve as definitive reference answers
* Audit AI-Generated Code — Evaluate model outputs using libraries like Scikit-Learn, PyTorch, and TensorFlow for correctness, efficiency, and best practices
* Identify Reasoning Failures — Spot and document logical flaws in AI reasoning — data leakage, overfitting, improper handling of imbalanced datasets — and provide structured feedback to improve model behavior
* Work Independently — Complete task-based assignments asynchronously, fully on your own schedule

**Who You Are**

* Currently pursuing or holding a Masters or PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, or a quantitative field with a strong emphasis on data analysis
* Solid foundational knowledge across core areas such as supervised/unsupervised learning, deep learning, big data technologies (Spark/Hadoop), or NLP
* Able to communicate complex algorithmic concepts and statistical findings clearly and concisely in writing
* Precise and detail-oriented — you notice when code logic, mathematical notation, or statistical conclusions don't hold up
* No prior AI or data annotation experience required

**Nice to Have**

* Experience with data annotation, data quality assurance, or evaluation systems
* Familiarity with production-level data science workflows — MLOps, CI/CD for models, or model monitoring
* Background in academic research, technical writing, or peer review
* Hands-on experience with experiment tracking tools like MLflow or Weights & Biases

**Why Join Us**

* Work directly with industry-leading AI research labs on genuinely cutting-edge models
* Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
* Freelance autonomy with the structure of meaningful, high-impact technical work
* Engage deeply with topics at the frontier of machine learning and AI development
* Potential for ongoing work and contract extension as new projects launch

The Team
  
  
You will join a dynamic AI Infrastructure team focused on enabling high-performance AI across Zoom's products and services. The team builds the core systems that support model training, deployment, and inference at scale, driving innovation in areas such as real-time communication, computer vision, and natural language understanding.
  
  
What you can expect
  
  
You will build and optimize the inference systems that serve Zoom's AI models in production. Working alongside senior inference engineers, research and platform teams, you will profile serving workloads, find the bottlenecks that limit latency, throughput and cost, and ship the fixes. You will work close to the metal: inside inference frameworks, GPU profiles and serving infrastructure.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Build, tune and maintain components of Zoom's inference serving stack for transformer and multimodal models, including large and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures
* Implement and evaluate inference optimisations such as speculative decoding, continuous batching, KV cache management, parallelism layouts and quantisation (INT4/INT8/FP8)
* Extend and customise inference frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or equivalent) to support new models and Zoom's production requirements
* Profile GPU workloads with Nsight Systems or equivalent tools, root-cause performance regressions, and validate improvements with reproducible benchmarks
* Build and improve internal tooling for benchmarking, performance modelling and serving configuration
* Partner with researchers to bring new model architectures into production efficiently
* Contribute to on-call and production support for the services you build, with guidance from senior engineers

What we're looking for
  
  

* A degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related field (MS or PhD preferred), or equivalent practical experience
* 0–3 years of software engineering experience; internships, research and open-source work in ML systems count
* Hands-on experience with at least one inference framework (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM or ONNX Runtime), at the level of serving and modifying it, not only exporting models
* Working knowledge of how LLM inference performs on GPUs: memory bandwidth, KV cache, batching, and communication across GPUs
* Experience profiling and debugging GPU performance, with evidence of an optimisation you measured and shipped
* Depth in at least one of: speculative decoding, continuous batching, KV cache design, quantisation, distributed or multi-GPU serving
* Strong programming skills in Python and C++, and comfort reading and changing large framework codebases

**Preferred**

* Merged contributions to vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, PyTorch or similar projects
* CUDA, Triton or CUTLASS kernel development
* Experience serving MoE or 100B+ parameter models, or multi-node inference (NCCL, RDMA/RoCE)
* Graduate coursework or research in ML systems, compilers or high-performance computing

**Job Description**
The HPC Software & Storage Engineering Strategist is a senior individual contributor reporting directly to the Vice President of HPC Software & Storage Engineering. This role serves as a strategic advisor and operating partner to the VP and leadership team, providing analysis, planning, and organizational insight to inform workforce, investment, portfolio, and operating decisions.
  
  
The Strategist will develop and maintain an integrated, forward-looking view of the organization’s workforce, financial investments, engineering capacity, product, and sustaining obligations. The role will translate business and technology strategy into resource and investment requirements and provide leadership with clear recommendations regarding where to invest, rebalance, consolidate, or reduce investment.
  
  
This individual will work across Engineering, Finance, Product Management, Business Planning, Support, and other key stakeholders to ensure organizational resources are aligned with the HPC & AI strategy and roadmap.
  
  
The role is expected to move beyond reporting and analysis to identify trends, challenge assumptions, evaluate alternatives, and recommend actions.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Workforce & Capacity Strategy**

* Own and maintain the HPC Software & Storage Engineering headcount forecast, including monthly actuals, forecasts, hiring plans, attrition assumptions, open positions, and organizational changes.
* Develop and implement multi-year workforce and capacity models aligned with technology roadmaps, product commitments, platform schedules, sustaining requirements, and strategic priorities.
* Work with the directors on future engineering commitments into required skills, capacity, and headcount.
* Identify capacity gaps, skill gaps, organizational constraints, and areas of over- or under-investment.
* Evaluate workforce allocation across new product development, platform enablement, sustaining, technical debt, and strategic initiatives.
* Develop recommendations for resource reallocation and investment based on organizational priorities.
* Model alternative workforce scenarios to support leadership decisions.

**CAPEX, OPEX & Investment Strategy**

* Lead and implement the planning and management process for HPC Software & Storage Engineering CAPEX and OPEX.
* Partner with Finance and engineering leadership to develop annual budgets, long-range plans, forecasts, and investment scenarios.
* Maintain visibility into actual and forecast spending relative to plan.
* Identify material variances, emerging risks, and opportunities and recommend corrective actions.
* Connect engineering investments to strategic priorities, roadmap deliverables, and expected business outcomes.
* Evaluate the financial implications of alternative roadmap, staffing, sourcing, and organizational decisions.
* Provide leadership with recommendations regarding investment tradeoffs when resources are constrained.

**Sustaining & Support Economics**

* Represent HPC Software R&D’s interests and requirements in defining software support policies, support durations, sustaining models, and funding requirements.
* Establish an integrated view of the engineering resources consumed by sustaining and support obligations.
* Evaluate sustaining headcount requirements against funding and capacity provided by the Support organization.
* Quantify the cost to Engineering of delivering long-term product support and identify unfunded or underfunded obligations.
* Assess whether support funding and staffing are commensurate with the engineering effort required to meet customer and contractual commitments.
* Develop and implement agreed-upon recommendations regarding support duration, funding models, staffing levels, product lifecycle transitions, and end-of-support decisions.
* Identify legacy products or commitments consuming disproportionate engineering capacity and make the associated investment tradeoffs visible to leadership.
* Partner with Support, Product Management, Finance, and Engineering to establish sustainable support and funding models.

**Portfolio Investment Strategy**

* Develop an integrated view of where HPC Software & Storage Engineering resources and dollars are invested across the portfolio.
* Evaluate investment across strategic development, platform enablement, sustaining, technical debt, infrastructure, and other engineering commitments.
* Assess whether current investment aligns with the organization’s strategic priorities and future roadmap.
* Identify areas where investment should be increased, maintained, consolidated, reduced, or exited.
* Evaluate the opportunity cost of continuing lower-priority or legacy investments.
* Provide fact-based recommendations to support portfolio prioritization and resource allocation.
* Establish mechanisms to measure whether investments are producing the intended engineering and business outcomes.

**Long-Range Strategic Planning**

* Translate the HPC & AI technology and product strategy into multi-year workforce, capacity, and financial requirements.
* Develop 12-, 24-, and 36-month views of organizational demand and investment requirements.
* Identify future resource constraints and investment needs early enough to enable leadership action.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders to understand upcoming technologies, platforms, and roadmap transitions and their implications for the organization.
* Integrate workforce, financial, sustaining, and portfolio assumptions into long-range planning.
* Develop scenarios that enable leadership to understand the consequences of alternative strategic choices.

**Organizational & Scenario Modeling**

* Develop organizational scenarios to evaluate alternative structures, sourcing approaches, geographic strategies, and resource allocations.
* Assess the financial, capacity, execution, and organizational implications of proposed changes.
* Model make/buy/partner decisions where appropriate.
* Provide objective analysis to support organizational design and investment decisions.

**Strategic Analysis & Executive Decision Support**

* Serve as a strategic thought partner to the VP and leadership team on organizational, workforce, financial, and investment decisions.
* Develop analyses that connect headcount, spending, engineering capacity, roadmap commitments, sustaining obligations, and business priorities.
* Identify trends and emerging risks before they materially affect execution.
* Frame complex decisions by clearly articulating alternatives, tradeoffs, risks, and recommended actions.
* Challenge assumptions and provide an independent, data-driven perspective.
* Develop concise executive-level materials for strategic planning, business reviews, portfolio reviews, and investment decisions.
* Track major strategic decisions and evaluate whether the expected outcomes are being achieved.

**Organizational Planning & Operating Rhythm**

* Establish and maintain a consistent operating cadence for workforce, financial, portfolio, and strategic planning.
* Create a trusted source of information for organizational capacity, investment, commitments, and risks.
* Improve forecasting accuracy, data quality, and visibility across the organization.
* Ensure leadership decisions are translated into updated workforce and investment plans.
* Drive follow-through on actions resulting from strategic and investment reviews.

**What Success Looks Like**
The Strategist creates the fact-base and strategic insight that allow the VP and leadership team to answer:
  
  

* Where are our people and dollars invested today?
* Are those investments aligned with our highest strategic priorities?
* What capabilities and capacity will we need over the next three years?
* Where are we over-invested or under-invested?
* How much engineering capacity is being consumed by sustaining and legacy commitments?
* Are our support obligations appropriately funded?
* What are we receiving in return for the resources Engineering dedicates to Support?
* Which investments should we increase, maintain, consolidate, reduce, or stop?
* What is the opportunity cost of continuing existing commitments?
* What are the workforce and financial implications of our roadmap?
* If our available resources change, what should we prioritize and what should we stop doing?

Success is not measured by producing reports. It is measured by enabling better decisions, earlier identification of risks and investment gaps, stronger alignment of resources to strategy, and improved return on the organization’s engineering investment.
  
  
**Qualifications**

* Significant experience in strategy, engineering operations, business planning, financial planning, portfolio management, or related leadership roles within a complex technology organization.
* Demonstrated ability to advise and influence senior executives and engineering leaders.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including workforce modeling, CAPEX/OPEX planning, forecasting, investment analysis, and scenario modeling.
* Experience translating technology and product strategies into workforce and investment requirements.
* Strong analytical capability with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex organizational and financial information into actionable recommendations.
* Ability to understand complex engineering organizations, technology roadmaps, and product lifecycle considerations.
* Exceptional executive communication and presentation skills.
* Ability to influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority.
* Demonstrated judgment and comfort challenging assumptions and presenting alternative perspectives to senior leadership.
* Experience in large-scale software, infrastructure, systems, HPC, AI, or enterprise technology environments preferred.

**Leadership Characteristics**
The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking, business and financial acumen, analytical rigor, and a strong understanding of how engineering organizations operate.
  
  
This individual is intellectually curious, comfortable working with ambiguity, and able to move fluidly between detailed analysis and executive-level strategic thinking. They do not simply report what is happening; they determine what it means, why it matters, and what leadership should do about it.
  
  
**The Strategist’s Central Question Is**
**Are we investing our people, dollars, and engineering capacity in the right places to deliver our strategy—and if not, what should we change?**

**Description**
Amazon runs one of the world’s most complex eCommerce platforms, where operational efficiency directly drives profitability and customer satisfaction. Efficiency is core to Amazon’s DNA, reflected in the Leadership Principle of Frugality and the Flywheel strategy that lowers cost structures to fuel growth. With the cost of operating Amazon’s global infrastructure measured in billions of dollars, achieving true economies of scale rather than allowing scale to increase costs is essential to our success.
  
  
The Alloy team serves as Amazon’s central efficiency organization, leading company-wide cost optimization through intelligent and automated use of AWS resources. **About The Role**
What if your expertise in machine learning, statistical inference, and data engineering could directly shape how the world's most advanced AI systems reason through complex problems? We're looking for data scientists with graduate-level training to challenge, audit, and refine cutting-edge AI models — exposing their blind spots and building them into more reliable, rigorous tools.
  
  
This is a fully remote, flexible contract role. No prior AI industry experience required — just deep, hands-on command of data science and the ability to think critically about how models reason.
  
  

* Organization: Alignerr
* Type: Hourly Contract
* Location: Remote
* Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

**What You'll Do**

* Design Advanced Challenges — Develop complex, domain-specific data science problems spanning hyperparameter optimization, Bayesian inference, cross-validation strategies, dimensionality reduction, and more
* Author Ground-Truth Solutions — Write rigorous, step-by-step technical solutions — including Python/R scripts, SQL queries, and mathematical derivations — that serve as the gold standard for evaluating AI outputs
* Audit AI-Generated Code — Evaluate AI-produced code using libraries like Scikit-Learn, PyTorch, and TensorFlow for technical accuracy, efficiency, and correctness
* Sharpen AI Reasoning — Identify logical failures in AI outputs — data leakage, overfitting, improper handling of imbalanced datasets — and deliver structured feedback that improves how models think

**Who You Are**

* Solid foundational knowledge across core areas such as supervised/unsupervised learning, deep learning, big data technologies (Spark, Hadoop), or NLP
* Able to communicate complex algorithmic concepts and statistical findings clearly and concisely in writing
* Naturally precise — you catch errors in code syntax, mathematical notation, and statistical logic that others overlook
* Self-directed and reliable when working independently on task-based assignments
* No prior AI or data annotation experience required

**Nice to Have**

* Prior experience with data annotation, data quality assurance, or AI evaluation systems
* Familiarity with production-level data science workflows — MLOps, CI/CD for models, or similar
* Hands-on experience across multiple modelling domains or industry verticals
* Background in academic research or technical writing

**Why Join Us**

* Work directly with industry-leading AI research labs on frontier model development
* Fully remote and asynchronous — work when and where it suits you
* Freelance autonomy with meaningful, intellectually engaging work
* High-impact contributions: your expertise directly shapes how advanced AI systems reason about data science
* Potential for ongoing contracts and project renewals as new AI initiatives launch

* Ability to assess quantitative problems carefully and identify errors in analysis, assumptions, or interpretation.

**Forward Deployed Engineer, Healthcare**

As Protege expands its healthcare business, customers and data partners need tailored implementation support and technical expertise in complex, regulated environments. This role is critical to accelerating customer and data partner outcomes, ensuring success across a growing portfolio of engagements, and identifying repeatable implementation patterns that can become scalable product capabilities.
  
  
This role sits at the center of a vertical that is growing extremely rapidly. **Own healthcare customer engagements end-to-end**

* Lead technical work from initial scoping through implementation, data ingestion, and continued refreshes.
* Become the primary technical partner for assigned healthcare data partners.
* Build trusted relationships with customer engineering and technical teams.
* Manage multiple concurrent healthcare engagements while maintaining quality and customer confidence.

**Build custom solutions for complex customer needs**

* Develop and deploy integrations, data transformations, and applications that solve customer-specific challenges.
* Navigate customer technical environments and adapt Protege’s platform capabilities to real-world deployment constraints.

**The Role**
You will build and ship LLM-powered features and agentic workflows for our customers. These features automate the routine parts of a claim and guide customers on the rest, so they have to earn that trust with measured accuracy, not a convincing demo. Agents run as steps inside deterministic workflows, and privacy and security are design baselines, not review gates. Agentic coding tools are how you move fast. What you add is what they are worst at: system design, security, and hard debugging. You own features end to end.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Ship LLM-powered features and agentic workflows in Python and TypeScript, from a problem scoped with product managers and data scientists through production traffic, and help set the metrics you will be measured against.
* Write the evals, guardrails, and feedback loops that make your features trustworthy, and hold them to explicit token and latency budgets.
* Use agentic coding tools every day, and own the review of what they produce: catch the correctness, security, and design problems in generated code before you open the pull request.
* Maintain and extend the NLP pipelines that turn unstructured claim data into structured data customers can act on, blending semantic search, classical NLP, and LLMs.
* Build and operate durable, event-driven services in which agents run as steps inside deterministic workflows, with checkpointed model outputs so a retry does not re-invoke a completed LLM step.
* Trace every model call and agent step so a recommendation can be reconstructed and audited, with citations back to the source documents, and wire that tracing into your alerts.
* Model and query claims data across relational, document, and graph stores.
* Design privacy and security in from the start: tenant isolation, least-privilege access for agents and their tools, and a clear rule for what data may reach a model provider.
* Write a technical design document before any significant change, and use it to get feedback and buy-in from the team before you build.
* Take part in a shared on-call rotation for the services you build.

**Requirements**

* 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, including at least one LLM-powered feature you shipped and then operated in production.
* Python and TypeScript: typed, tested, async code in both, and real depth in one.
* Evals you have designed for LLM output, plus guardrails you have shipped.
* A clear account of how you constrain an agentic coding tool's context and verify its output, from daily use of Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or similar on production work.
* Pipelines that blend LLMs with semantic search and classical NLP: structured output, tool calling, embedding-based retrieval, and a case where a classical technique beat an LLM.
* Services built on message- or event-driven architectures, including long-running workflows with retries, idempotent handlers, and event-sourced state, plus an LLM or agent step you ran inside one.
* Data modeling and development across relational, document, and graph databases such as PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Neo4j, including when each type fits and the partition-key, consistency, and tenant-isolation calls you made.
* Backend services built and operated on Azure or AWS, and exposure to a durable workflow engine such as Temporal or the Durable Task Scheduler.
* Technical design documents you have written to get feedback and buy-in from a team before building, and that the team then built to.
* Clear writing and discussion for technical and non-technical audiences, and code review you can give as well as take.

**Even Better If You Have**

* React and TypeScript experience, so you can deliver a full-stack feature end to end. Chat, streaming, and citation-heavy AI experiences especially.
* Experience with CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code such as Terraform or Bicep.
* Experience with agent frameworks, LangGraph and the Microsoft Agent Framework among them, and with the ways agents reach their tools: the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, command-line tools, and microservices.
* Experience with LLM observability and evaluation tooling such as LangSmith, Arize, or Braintrust, and with OpenTelemetry-based tracing.
* Experience designing A/B tests for AI features, or what-if simulations that replay historical claims through a proposed change before it ships.
* Exposure to the insurance, claims, or automotive repair domains.

**What Success Looks Like**

* In your first six months you ship an LLM-powered feature, its evals run in CI, and you can name the metric it moved.
* When a model migration or prompt change causes a regression, the evals you wrote catch it before a customer does.
* You take ownership from concept to production with light direction, asking the right questions early.
* You care that things hold up: the services you build survive retries, partial failures, and model migrations without incidents a customer can see.
* When something goes wrong in production, the trace tells you which step and which model call, and you can show an auditor the same thing.
* Privacy and security reviews of your features find nothing that was not already designed in.
* You enjoy the craft, and it shows: engineers pick up your patterns without being told to.
* You enjoy the back-and-forth that gets a feature scoped, and you can argue a position without needing to win it.
* You embrace our ambitious, collaborative, and empathetic values, and you like problems where the answer has to be measured rather than argued.

Supports the development and evaluation of AI pilots — including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agentic workflows — and helps translate business needs into feasible technical approaches. Assists in identifying and advising on potential AI use cases across the Division, working with senior S&R leaders and other stakeholders. This is a greenfield engineering role. You will help establish the architecture, design the data model, ship the first services, and set the patterns the rest of the platform will inherit. 
  
  
Expect a zero-to-one cadence. Design an API contract in the morning, ship a Postgres migration before lunch, push a Bicep change to staging by end of day. We optimize for engineers who can hold the full stack in their head, make sound architectural decisions, and ship working software at pace.

**The Role at a Glance:**

* *Scope*
  : Schema to UI: Database design, API contracts, frontend components, infrastructure. No tier is off-limits.
* *Surface*
  : Greenfield build: Property management platform built from scratch. Multi-tenant from day one. Operator tooling, leasing, accounting, capital markets.
* *Cadence*
  : Zero to one: Trunk-based development, short-lived branches, feature flags, working software in staging on a daily rhythm.
* *Impact*
  : Foundational: What you ship in the first year becomes how the platform works for the next ten.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **React surfaces**
  : First-generation operator and resident-facing applications. React 18 with TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query v5, React Hook Form, Zod. Component composition against the PDS Foundation design system. The patterns set here will be inherited by every surface that follows.
* **Service layer**
  : TypeScript services on Node 20 LTS with NestJS or Express. OpenAPI contracts shared with the front end through code generation. JWT and OAuth flows, RBAC enforcement, structured audit logs, request-scoped tracing. The shared libraries that every future service will depend on.
* **Postgres data model**
  : Multi-tenant schema design on Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Tenant isolation strategy, normalization tradeoffs, index strategy from day one, audit trails baked into the data model. Migrations through Prisma or Knex.
* **Warehouse integration**
  : Stand up change data capture from Postgres into the Bronze layer of Enzo, our medallion warehouse. Establish read models surfaced from Gold-layer views back into product. Contract-first design with the data team.
* **Event-driven backbone**
  : Asynchronous workflows over Azure Service Bus. Idempotent consumers, dead-letter handling, exactly-once where the business requires it. The async patterns the rest of the platform will adopt.
* **Infrastructure and Observability**
  : Bicep modules for App Service, Functions, Container Apps, Service Bus, Key Vault, and managed identities. Multi-stage Azure DevOps pipelines. Structured logs, OpenTelemetry, and SLO definitions in place before we ever take production traffic.
* **Stack**
  :
  + *Front End*
    : React 18 + TypeScript 5
    - React 18 with Suspense and concurrent features, TypeScript 5.x strict, Vite, TanStack Query v5, React Hook Form with Zod, the PDS Foundation design system through Figma MCP.
  + *Back End*
    : Node 20 + NestJS
    - Node 20 LTS, NestJS or Express, TypeScript strict mode, Prisma against Postgres, BullMQ on Redis for background work, OpenAPI 3.x contracts generated for both sides.
  + *Data*
    : Azure Postgres + Fabric
    - Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Azure Data Factory for orchestration, Microsoft Fabric lakehouse with Bronze/Silver/Gold layers, Power BI Premium, Python and PySpark on the data team.
  + *Cloud*
    : Microsoft Azure
    - App Service Premium, Function Apps, Container Apps, Service Bus with sessions, Key Vault with managed identities, Application Insights, Front Door Premium, private endpoints throughout.
  + *Devops*
    : GitHub + Azure DevOps
    - GitHub for source and PR review, Azure DevOps multi-stage YAML pipelines for CI/CD. Trunk-based development, required reviews, automated test gates, environment promotion via parameters.
  + *Infrastructure*
    : Bicep + Terraform
    - Bicep modules for first-party Azure, Terraform for cross-cloud and third-party providers. Remote state in Azure Storage with locking, drift detection in pipelines.

**Qualifications:**

* **Required:**
  + Five-plus years in production: building web applications. You have taken a system from greenfield to production, or rebuilt the foundations of one that needed it.
  + TypeScript depth: generics, conditional types, discriminated unions, branded types. You know when to reach for them and when to stop.
  + React expertise: hooks, render optimization, error boundaries, Suspense. You can diagnose a re-render storm and you've written a custom hook that earned its keep.
  + Production Node.js: event loop awareness, streaming and backpressure, memory profiling, graceful shutdown, structured logging.
  + Relational data modeling: schema design, normalization tradeoffs, index strategy, partitioning, query plan analysis. You catch N+1 in code review.
  + API design: REST conventions, idempotency, versioning, pagination, OpenAPI specifications, authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT, session).
  + Azure or equivalent: production experience with App Service, Functions, identity, networking, observability. AWS or GCP at the same depth is fine.
  + CI/CD and IaC discipline: pipeline-as-code, environment promotion, automated test gates, infrastructure as reviewed artifacts, no clicks in the portal.
* **Preferred**
  :
  + Postgres extensions in production: pg\_stat\_statements, pgvector, pgcrypto, PostGIS, logical replication.
  + Lakehouse and BI tooling at production scale: Microsoft Fabric, Power BI Premium with DAX, Python and PySpark on the data plane.
  + Event-sourced architectures, CQRS, sagas, or domain-driven design applied to a real codebase.
  + LLM-assisted engineering: Claude Code, Cursor, or retrieval-augmented internal tooling shipped to other engineers.
  + Real estate, property management, financial services, or other regulated-industry domain experience.
  + RUST development experience.

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering/development, Computer Science, or related field.
  
  
1-3 years of experience in software development.
  
  
Strong proficiency in Python (3.12+) backend development — FastAPI, Pydantic v2, async/await — and T-SQL, with deep comfort in the data and service layers of an enterprise application.
  
  
Expert-level SQL Server and data engineering: parameterized query authoring, query optimization and execution-plan analysis, indexing strategy, set-based processing, and bulk / ETL data movement and large-dataset performance tuning — plus comfort migrating logic out of legacy stored procedures into Python.
  
  
Exposure to modern cloud data platforms and warehouses (e.g. Snowflake) and an interest in integrating multiple, heterogeneous data sources — each just another SQLAlchemy dialect — behind a unified API.

Join a new digital R&D function within an established residential construction business. Alongside an existing product delivery organization of approximately 220 people, the team will explore new AI capabilities and test which ideas merit further investment.

A pipeline of 27 use cases is ready for evaluation. The business already uses AI for construction takeoffs, turning floor plans into bills of materials in minutes rather than hours. This team will investigate further opportunities through rapid, practical experimentation.

**How the Team Works**

You will work in a dedicated team of two or three AI and full stack engineers. Each 10-working-day cycle takes a use case through discovery, checkpoints, and a working prototype, ending with a clear decision to proceed or stop. Successful concepts pass to product teams for production development, and the R&D team begins the next cycle. Success means reaching a sound decision quickly, including identifying ideas that should be stopped.

* Build working prototypes using AI capabilities and the application stack appropriate to each experiment.
* Apply AI tools across the development lifecycle, from specification and implementation through testing and review.
* Validate AI-generated code and outputs against specifications, identifying errors, gaps, and limitations.
* Use prepared data products, demonstrate findings at checkpoints, and support the final decision to proceed or stop.
* Hand over promising concepts and technical findings so product teams can develop production-ready solutions.

**Experience and Capabilities**

We are seeking hands-on engineers with evidence of building products or experimenting rapidly. Practical examples and technical judgment are central to the assessment.

For both roles, you should bring:

* Experience taking an idea from discovery to a demonstrable prototype in a fast-moving product environment.
* The ability to write clear, comprehensive specifications and verify that AI-assisted development delivers the intended behavior.
* A practical understanding of AI capabilities, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and the relationship between AI and machine learning.
* Confidence using AI tools, such as Claude, throughout the software development lifecycle and critically reviewing their output.

A six-month contract-to-hire structure is being considered; final duration and terms are to be agreed.

The target is to complete the first prototype cycle before mid-December. A second team in Latin America or another nearshore location is also being considered.

**About Us**
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
  
  
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
  
  
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
  
  
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
  
  
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
  
  
****The Job****
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
  
  
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
  
  
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
  
  
**About You**

* You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
* You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.

* You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.

* You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
* You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
* You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.

****Nice to have:****

* Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.

* Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
* Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

* Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
* Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
* Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
* Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
* Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

* Dscout AI Training & Evals

Dscout AI Training & Evals builds human data and evals that show whether AI works for real people. For ten years Dscout has captured how people behave in real context, with consent and scientific rigor. AI Training & Evals points that engine at AI: consented human behavior and judgment, turned into the training data, evals, and benchmarks AI teams trust.
  
  
Capability has outrun trust. Models ace benchmarks and still surprise people in the wild. A benchmark says how capable a model is. It does not say whether the model works for the person using it, across weeks, in the mess of real life. That gap is where we work.
  
  
We serve AI researchers, the product builders who ship alongside them, and the research teams who partner with both. We are a new unit inside an established company: live customers, a mature platform (React, Elixir, Python, Swift, Kotlin; SOC 2 and HITRUST certified), a small senior team, and room to build. We work AI-native. Agents write code, evals gate changes, and we aim to do in months what used to take years.
  
  
*A note from our Chief AI Officer & GM.*
The questions that matter most about AI are not answered by a bigger leaderboard. Does a model work for a real person across three weeks of real use? Does a rubric measure what it claims? Does an AI judge agree with the people it stands for? We have a decade of methods for studying people in real context, and we will publish our methods and benchmarks so the field can check our work. Join us to do rigorous science that matters.
  
  
**Why this seat**

* Work on a problem the field has not solved: measuring whether AI works for real people, over real time.
* Study something most evals do not have: real participants, doing real tasks in their own context.
* Own the benchmark. You are founding it, not joining a team that has one.
* Publish. Methods and benchmarks go to the research community, with first authorship on the benchmark.
* Join a small senior team with direct access to the Head of AI Research and the GM.
* Job Description

This is a research-first role focused on questions where the right rubric, benchmark, or method does not yet exist. You will find the gaps, propose bold directions, and take projects from first hypothesis through experiments and benchmark construction to publication. You will also build: the science has to run inside live customer programs.
  
  
**What you will do**
*Rubrics and QA science*

* Design rubrics and test whether they measure what they claim: validity, reliability, and sensitivity.
* Measure how reliable human raters are, and when disagreement is noise versus real signal.
* Calibrate AI judges against real human judgment, and study when they drift away from it.
* Build quality signals that put evidence behind every data point we ship.

*Long-horizon, real-user benchmarks*

* Design Dscout's first benchmark: real users, in real context, over long horizons. Multi-week tasks across tools, not one-shot prompts.
* Define the protocol, task design, scoring, and release. Work with our delivery team on fieldwork.
* Work out how to keep a living benchmark honest over time: drift, contamination, difficulty, and what counts as a meaningful change.
* Write the paper and own the public release.

*Human judgment as training and eval signal*

* Study when real-world human feedback improves a model and when it adds noise.
* Explore how preference and judgment data from representative people differ from expert data.
* Turn findings into methods our forward deployed engineers and delivery team can run in the field.

*New research directions*

* These areas are the core, not the whole list. You will have significant latitude to propose new programs, such as calibrating user simulations against real behavior, human-AI collaboration, and behavioral evaluation of agents.
* Co-author with outside labs and academics on studies that need real-user data. Help run our paper-reading group.

**A good first year**

* A QA and rubric framework running on live customer programs, with documented validity.
* Benchmark v0 released, with a paper submitted to a top venue.
* At least one external team using or citing our work.
* Delivery colleagues using your methods without needing you in the room.

**How we will hire:**
a conversation with the Head of AI Research; a research talk on a project you led; a design exercise (how would you validate a rubric for a long-horizon task?); a conversation with the GM, forward deployed engineers, and delivery partners.
  
  

* Requirements

**What we care about most.**
A strong publication record helps. We care most about whether you can find the question that matters, design a rigorous way to answer it, and move fast enough that the answer is still useful.
  
  
**What you bring**

* Published research, or strong preprints and workshop papers, in evals, preference learning, reward modeling, human-AI interaction, measurement, or agent evaluation.
* A PhD, a PhD in progress, or an MS with two or more strong research internships at labs or top industry groups. If you do not have advanced degrees but have a history of creative machine learning research work, this is just as desirable.
* Strong applied statistics: inter-rater reliability, confidence intervals, power, and a nose for when a metric misleads.

* Experience running experiments on messy human data, not only curated datasets.
* Clear technical writing, and the ability to explain your work to a lab researcher and to a product manager.
* Based in the Bay Area.

**Nice to have:**
long-horizon or agentic evaluation work; psychometrics, item response theory, or human-subjects research; open-source benchmark or dataset contributions.

**Job Description**
AI Security Incubation & Innovation
  
  
Security and Risk Engineering
  
  
**About The Team**
The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning.
  
  
This is a zero-to-one incubation. We're building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability (where an attacker could realistically get in) rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and you'll help build it.
  
  
The role
  
  
As an ML Engineer, you'll build and ship LLM-powered features for a new exploitability engine. That means the services, retrieval pipelines and agent workflows that turn raw security signal into ranked, reachable attack paths. You'll work on well-scoped problems with senior engineers, learn how production AI systems are built and run, and take on more ownership as you grow.
  
  
What you'll own
  
  

* Well-scoped features and components, from design to production, with guidance from senior engineers.
* The quality of what you ship: tests, evals and monitoring that show your work does what it should.
* Pieces of the AI plumbing, such as prompts, retrieval, tool integrations and data connectors, and keeping them reliable.
* LLMs/Agentic AI and MLOps are relevant, let's include those

What you'll do
  
  

* Build backend services and APIs in Python that connect LLMs to enterprise security data.
* Build LLM features using prompt engineering, structured outputs, tool/function calling, and retrieval (RAG, embeddings, vector search).
* Help build and extend agent workflows that retrieve information, call tools, and recover from failures.
* Write evals and automated tests that measure accuracy, latency and cost.
* Build connectors that bring security evidence (vulnerability scanners, identity systems, asset inventories) into the platform.
* Use AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Devin every day, and review their output carefully.
* Prototype quickly to test new AI capabilities against real security problems.
* Take part in code and design reviews, and learn the security domain from security R&D and SecOps partners.
* What you bring
* Strong Python. This is a must.
* Solid software engineering fundamentals: data structures, APIs, testing, debugging.
* Hands-on experience building something with LLMs, at work or in a substantial project: RAG, embeddings, tool calling or agents.
* Experience calling at least one frontier model API or SDK (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or equivalent).
* Curiosity about security and a willingness to learn the domain on the job.
* Clear communication, and comfort asking questions in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
* You don't need a background in classical ML, statistics or data science.
* Nice to have
* Experience with AWS, Azure or GCP, containers, or CI/CD.
* Exposure to AI evaluation, observability or guardrails.
* Experience with vector databases or search.
* Any exposure to security: vulnerability management, identity, threat detection, CTFs or coursework.
* Open-source contributions.

**Qualifications**
Qualifications
  
  

* 2+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience.
* Strong programming experience in Python.
* Experience building or integrating LLM-powered applications, in production or in substantial projects.
* Working knowledge of APIs, databases and cloud-native development.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

What success looks like
  
  

* Ship: Take a scoped feature from ticket to production with tests and evals in place.
* Build AI-native: Choose the right LLM technique for a problem, and know when not to use one.
* Learn fast: Get productive in the codebase and the security domain quickly.
* Grow: Need less guidance over time and take on bigger parts of the system.

**Job Description:**

**About PointFive**
PointFive finds the cost buried inside enterprise infrastructure, from the cloud to coding agents. We pioneered DeepWaste across cloud and data platforms, and we are now doing the same for AI token spend with TokenShift.
  
  
Fanatics, H&M, Hertz, Nubank, Citizens Bank and other Fortune 500 companies use PointFive to see and cut what their infrastructure and AI actually cost.
  
  
We have raised $96 million, most recently a $60 million Series B led by Accel. Engineering sits in Tel Aviv and our go-to-market team is focused on North America. PointFive Labs, our research arm, publishes original work on how infrastructure and AI actually get paid for.
  
  
CRN named us one of the 10 hottest cloud computing startups of 2026, Forbes Israel put us on its Next Billion Dollar Startups list, and Redpoint selected us for its InfraRed 100, its ranking of the private companies shaping the future of cloud infrastructure.
  
  
**About The Role**
As PointFive’s first AI Engineer, Support Automation, you’ll own technical support for our enterprise customers. You’ll design and build an agentic solution to triage, diagnose, and resolve customer issues end to end. You’ll also measure how well it’s working, and own the escalation path to Engineering for anything that needs a fix.
  
  
This is an individual contributor role with ownership of an entire function, based in our NYC office (hybrid).
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Design and build an agentic solution to resolve customer tickets end to end, from first response through diagnosis and resolution.
* Define what success looks like and build the measurement layer to track it (time to first response, time to resolution, CSAT).
* Work the escalations your agents can’t solve yet, then teach the system to handle them next time.
* Partner with Engineering and Product on recurring issues, routing confirmed bugs to Engineering’s coding agents with the context needed to fix them.
* Turn resolved tickets into self-serve documentation customers can use on their own.
* Feed support trends back into the product roadmap.

What We're Looking For
  
  
**Must-have**

* Shipped AI agents or LLM-powered tools with real users.
* Hands-on experience integrating and debugging APIs, webhooks, and data sources.
* Built evals to measure agent quality before and after shipping.
* Clear, concise writing for both customers and engineers.
* Ability to operate in a startup environment: adaptable, self-directed, and resourceful.

**Nice to have**

* Cloud or FinOps knowledge (AWS, Azure or GCP billing)
* Customer-facing technical experience (support, solutions, or forward deployed engineering)
* Hands-on experience with AI support tooling (Pylon, Intercom Fin, Zendesk AI or similar)

**Compensation & Benefits**

* Base Salary Range: $120,000 – $195,000. Actual salary will be based on job-related skills, experience, and location.
* Health, dental, vision (yes, all three!), equity in something early-stage and exciting, generous PTO, 401K, meal & commuter benefits, a team that will actually challenge you and much more

Why PointFive
  
  

* Founders with a track record: Built and sold IntSights to Rapid7. Backed by top-tier investors with deep conviction in this category.
* Category-defining product: DeepWaste detection and agentic remediation with clear, measurable ROI for both engineering and finance teams.
* Early-stage leverage: Your work directly shapes the product, the culture, and the go-to-market playbook.
* Own a function, not a queue: You'll build Technical Support from scratch as an AI system, on real enterprise data, with exec backing from day one.

Compensation Range: $120K - $195K

**About MeeBoss**

**About Us**
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
  
  
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
  
  
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
  
  
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
  
  
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
  
  
****The Job****
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
  
  
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
  
  
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
  
  
**About You**

* You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.

Join our Deloitte AI & Engineering team to transform technology platforms, drive innovation, and help make a significant impact on our clients' success. You'll work alongside talented professionals reimagining and reengineering operations and processes that are critical to businesses. Your contributions can help clients improve financial performance, accelerate new digital ventures, and fuel growth through innovation.
  
  
**Work You'll Do**
As a Center Delivery Senior Consultant, Software Engineering Solutions on the Engineering as a Service team, you will:
  
  

* Build agents against a layered SDK contract (shared types/tools, composable tools, thin agent shell, FastAPI + React surface)
* Keep business logic in composable skills rather than shells or routers
* Integrate LLMs through a multi-provider abstraction (Anthropic/Bedrock/OpenAI/Azure, extending to Vertex/OCI) behind a single sanitization + audit boundary so no raw client data leaves the worker
* Implement durable service boundaries (async persistence, object-storage artifacts, and a tamper-evident hash-chain audit trail per run)
* Enforce tenant isolation via Postgres RLS scoped sessions and author Alembic migrations (enum/DDL idempotency, RLS policies)
* Wire agents into an event-driven orchestrator with human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gates, exposing progress via async tasks (Celery/Redis) and WebSocket
* Ship behind mechanical architecture linting and CI, contributing new invariant checks

**A successful candidate would possess:**

* Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
* Effective written and verbal communication skills
* Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
* Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
* Ability to lead projects or workstreams
* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
* Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
* Ability to meet deadlines
* Ability to provide clear guidance to others

We help transform engineering teams, modernize technology, and deliver complex programs with a product engineering mindset. Our flexible delivery models - traditional teams, pools, or pods, are tailored for each client's needs, offering engineering-led Advise, Implement, & Operate capabilities to accelerate innovation.

The LA County Board of Supervisors recently declared a local state of emergency for homelessness , and the County is working to revise and expand our response to help all who are affected. We are looking for qualified and passionate individuals to help us in the mission of addressing issues like housing, mental health, and substance use. If you are looking for a new career that will directly benefit the population of LA County, this may be the opportunity for you.
  
  
The Department of Homeless Services and Housing is seeking qualified candidates to fill emergency Data Scientist Supervisor vacancies related to the homelessness crisis.
  
  
Under the emergency order, applicants who meet the requirements may be hired for an initial period of up to 90 days, with an opportunity for permanent County employment.
  
  
During your initial work period, you will be assessed on your work performance. This assessment will be weighted 100%.
  
  
Those who successfully pass the assessment will be considered for permanent appointment to the Data Scientist Supervisor position.
  
  
**Essential Job Functions**

* Plans, organizes, supervises, manages, and evaluates highly technical and complex assignments of the section; with staff, develops, implements, and monitors data science projects from inception to implementation to ensure that the objectives and desired outcomes are achieved, and that critical decisions are made in a timely manner.
* Plans, assigns, and reviews the work of data scientists and analysts to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with business needs; ensures that section products and services continue to perform as desired over time and directs updates and modifications to these as necessary.
* Collaborates with IT group and program managers to identify departmental or divisional business needs and issues of strategic importance; implements enhancements to existing systems, recommends alternative systems, and assists in developing and implementing new data engineering, data modeling, and data science solutions as appropriate.
* In conjunction with the governance board and executive committees, defines the overall vision and strategy for data analytics across the organization.
* Assists to develop, implement, and evaluate divisional/departmental initiatives, strategies, and operational objectives through deployment of big data; advocates for measurability in strategic planning and operations in order to build analytics and evaluation into program design on a foundational level.
* Evaluates, manages, and participates in all aspects of the section’s solution development, including quality assurance and maintenance of data sets integrated from multiple sources; exploratory data analysis; model creation, testing, and deployment; presentation of findings; and consultation with program managers regarding effective operationalization and model fidelity to improve business outcomes.
* Directs the development of technical reports, dashboards, data briefs, white papers, and publications, including advanced data visualization tools.
* Works with IT data engineers and architects to develop and maintain large-scale databases that meet high standards for completeness, accuracy, and utility; supervises and participates in quality control checks of data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) of large-scale, structured, unstructured, and streaming data.
* Advises divisional/departmental managers on opportunities and gaps in their current capabilities across data science technology and infrastructure; recommends plans for growth through adoption of new methods and technologies.
* Builds solutions that apply machine learning techniques to address complex business problems, derive actionable insights, and maximize decision-making confidence.
* Makes recommendations, develops technical infrastructure and analytic competencies, and participates in project selection to inform and execute the data science strategy of the County, department, or division.
* Stays current with and contributes to discovery of data science best practices; mentors staff and ensures the section maintains ongoing training and professional development and is competent in all techniques necessary to complete their duties; and participates in the broader data science community to identify and disseminate the latest developments in data and technology.
* Serves as a technical resource for divisional/departmental managers on data-driven program design and management and the translation of data science and knowledge into improved business outcomes, efficiency, and effectiveness of business processes.

For more information about the position, please visit this classification specification: Data Scientist Supervisor .

Amazon Web Services (AWS) provides companies of all sizes with an infrastructure web services platform in the cloud. A data lake enables you to break down data silos and combine different types of analytics to gain insights and guide better business decisions.
  
  
Joining the AWS Catalog organization gives you the opportunity to:

* Solve challenging problems that will revolutionize database computing in the cloud
* Build a product that will leverage the scale of resources available in the cloud
* Work for a company that’s a recognized leader in the cloud computing space
* Be involved in the fast growing, big data space

We are looking for developers with expertise and passion for building large-scale data-intensive systems and distributed systems. In particular, we are looking for developers that want to work on the next generation big data systems that will transform data management on AWS and across the industry.
  
  
Experience with large scale data analytics, big data platforms, highly available/fault tolerant systems, replicated data storage, and operating complex services running in the cloud are all pluses.

**Description**
Are you excited about building software that impacts millions of customers? Do you enjoy solving complex technical problems while collaborating with a talented team of engineers? We're looking for a Software Development Engineer II to join Amazon and help design, build, and operate systems that matter at scale.
  
  
In this role, you will contribute across the full software development lifecycle—from understanding customer needs and defining solutions to implementing, testing, deploying, and operating production software. You will tackle challenging problems where the business context is clear but the path forward requires creative, well-reasoned design. You will write high-quality, maintainable code and help raise the bar for your team through mentorship and thoughtful code reviews. If you are a self-starter who thrives on turning ambiguity into clarity and delivering meaningful results, we'd love to hear from you.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design and implement software solutions for major features and improvements, applying sound system design principles that account for scalability, maintainability, and performance.
* Write clean, well-tested, and maintainable code using optimal data structures and algorithms, and actively participate in code reviews to provide constructive feedback to teammates.
* Collaborate with customers, stakeholders, and cross-functional peers to understand business requirements and deliver solutions that balance customer needs with technical considerations.
* Identify and resolve root causes of operational issues, driving permanent fixes and continuously improving your team's operational health and processes.
* Mentor and coach fellow engineers, train new team members on system architecture and operations, and contribute to clear technical documentation that supports long-term team knowledge.

A day in the life
  
  
Your day begins by reviewing operational metrics and addressing any alerts from the systems you own. You then join your team's standup to align on priorities before diving into design or implementation work. You might spend the morning writing code for a new feature, then shift to reviewing a teammate's pull request in the afternoon—offering feedback that helps them grow. You regularly collaborate with product and engineering partners to refine requirements, and you evaluate opportunities to integrate generative AI tools where they can improve productivity.
  
  
**About The Team**
Our team is focused on building reliable, scalable software that directly improves the customer experience at Amazon. We value collaboration, continuous learning, and a commitment to operational excellence. Every engineer on the team has the opportunity to influence technical direction and contribute to meaningful projects.
  
  
We are building for the long term, investing in systems that are extensible and well-documented so they can evolve as customer needs change. If you're looking for an inclusive environment where your ideas are heard and your growth is supported, this is the team for you.
  
  
**Basic Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
* 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
* 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
* 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
* Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
